facts.text: Chester was founded in 1819 by an Ohio land company and named after Chester, England, becoming a trading center for wheat, corn, and soybeans.
The town’s first business was a general store opened in 1830 beside a castor oil press that later fed farmers with seed and growing methods.
Nathan Cole founded the Cole Milling Company in 1839, and his electric generator lit the town before Chicago had street lights.
During World War II, a local factory produced military boots primarily operated by women, keeping the town busy until its closure in the early 1960s.
The Menard Correctional Center, Illinois’s second‑oldest prison, was established in 1878 and remains a major part of Chester’s economy.
Charles Dickens visited Chester on April 11, 1842, and Mark Twain stayed at the town’s Cliff House while cruising the Mississippi.
